title: Can Statistics Tell Whether an Undeciphered Text Is Language? Calibrated Tests on the Voynich Manuscript
publication_action: Additive audit only; existing literature registry/site/frozen experiments were not changed. Do not add a duplicate record.

paper_facts.text: ZL3b: 37,554 tokens; IT2a: 36,736. Running, circular and radial text are included; six EVA groups are merged.
Shared word shapes use a trigram trained on full ZL word types; generated layouts follow ZL.
Each search uses 4,000 simulations, repeated twice: 22 fitted and 15 held-out statistics, with 100 predictive texts. These are held-out statistics, not held-out manuscript leaves.
Copy-T ports Timm rules, adding W-generated words and ZL-derived glyph-pair acceptance; Cipher-N uses Naibbe tables.
Boundary analysis measures glyph mutual information with position permutations and line-break checks.
Word-pair replication uses 300 frequent types, page shuffles, alternating ten-page blocks, near-copy exclusions and residual Spearman correlation.
Labels: 1,159 words, own-page versus randomized-page occurrence, Copy-H calibration, and 22 plant pairs.
Python/NumPy code is promised with publication. Bigram solvers, manuscript-derived tables, limited nomenclator settings and an after-the-fact combined rule restrict interpretation.
